topPRs.title: docs: roll the flag-reference generator out to op-node, op-proposer, op-challenger, op-conductor
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784185257434409)_

Tracks ethereum-optimism/solutions#971

## What

Rolls the flag-reference generator introduced in #21847 (op-batcher) out to the remaining first-party Go services, so every published flag catalog is generated from the urfave/cli definitions the binaries actually register, pinned to a finalized release:

| Component | Pinned tag | Visible flags | Tag↔develop flag sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| op-node | `op-node/v1.19.3` | 109 (3 required) | identical |
| op-proposer | `op-proposer/v1.16.3` | 54 (1 required) | moved on develop — generated at the tag |
| op-challenger | `op-challenger/v1.9.3` | 88 (4 required) | moved on develop — generated at the tag |
| op-conductor | `op-conductor/v0.9.4` | 61 (9 required) | moved on develop — generated at the tag |
| op-batcher | `op-batcher/v1.16.11` | 87 | unchanged from #21847 |

- **Pages reworked to import the snippets** (hand policy/context prose kept, hand-typed tables deleted): `node-operators/reference/op-node-config.mdx` (1,278→143 lines, was pinned to v1.10.2), `chain-operators/guides/configuration/proposer.mdx`, `chain-operators/tools/op-conductor/reference.mdx`. New page: `chain-operators/reference/challenger-configuration.mdx` (op-challenger had no flag catalog at all).
- **`-check` redesigned around a manifest `sha256` pin.** The components release independently, so develop's flag sources routinely sit past one component's tag while matching another's — byte-comparing a committed snippet against a regeneration from an arbitrary tree is only meaningful at the tag. `manifest.json` now records `{tag, sha256}` per snippet; `-check` fails on any snippet/manifest hash mismatch (hand-edit detection, valid at every commit) and reports current-tree parity informationally. New `-only {component}` flag supports per-tag regeneration. See the rewritten `scripts/gen-flags/README.md`, including the honest residual-gap list.
- **`canonicalizeUsage`**: the `--network` usage string enumerates the superchain-registry bundle's chain list, which changes with registry bumps independent of any release; the generator replaces the enumeration with a stable pointer so regeneration is byte-stable (documented deviation from raw `--help`).
- **`op-reth-config.mdx` retired to a pointer** at the imported op-reth CLI reference (`/rust/op-reth/cli/overview`, `/rust/op-reth/cli/op-reth/node`) — the 2,685-line hand copy was pinned to an old release and duplicated the imported surface. Six inbound per-flag anchor links re-pointed (snap-sync, reth-historical-proofs, archive-node, upgrade-19). No pages under `rust/op-reth/**` touched; the existing `op-geth-config` redirect still lands on a live page.
- **`generate-releases.ts`**: new `rewriteSpecsBlobLinks` transform canonicalizes specs-repo blob links in release bodies to the rendered specs site (outside code blocks only, idempotent); applied to the committed `releases/op-batcher.mdx`.
- Corrected from the old hand pages: `consensus.advertised` was documented as required but is optional in source; op-node's `--network`/`--rollup.config` exactly-one-of rule is now called out in prose (it is enforced by `CheckRequiredXor`, outside the required flag slice).

## Verification

An adversarial accuracy pass ran before this PR opened:

- All four snippets regenerate **byte-identical** at their tags (fresh worktree per tag, committed generator, run twice for determinism).
- Every flag row cross-checked against the actual `op-node` / `op-proposer` / `op-challenger` / `op-conductor` binaries built at the pinned tags: names, env vars, defaults match `--help` exactly; visible-flag sets match (hidden flags excluded on both sides); sampled usage strings match.
- Required mirrors verified against each tag's `flags.go` — including op-challenger's `l2-eth-rpc`, which `CheckRequired` enforces unconditionally from outside its required slice, and op-conductor's nine.
- `-check` is green for all five components; corrupting one committed snippet byte makes it fail on the sha256 pin.
- The pass found and fixed two release-accuracy errors in the prose (second commit): the challenger page listed a `game-proposal-outputs` subcommand that exists on develop but not in v1.9.3, and the op-reth pointer page claimed op-node defaults `--l2.enginekind` to `geth` when the source (tag and develop) defaults to `reth`.
- Lints: nav validator OK, redirect lint OK, link-policy lint clean against its baseline (pruned by exactly the two entries this diff resolves), `gofmt`/`go vet` clean.

## Notes for reviewers

1. **docs.json serialization**: this PR adds one nav line (the challenger reference page). Per the program rule, at most one docs.json-touching PR should be in flight at a time — rebase whichever of the open docs.json PRs merges second.
2. **Supersedes part of #21867**: the op-node-config rework deletes the Info block containing the pinned `receipts_rpc.go` link that #21867 re-points (one hunk there). Whichever merges second needs a trivial `lint-link-policy.baseline.json` rebase (also against #21866).
3. **Complementary to #21866**: that PR fixes the three release-page intro-string blob links at their source; this PR fixes the release-body link class in the generator. No overlap — an earlier duplicate fix here was reverted.

Reviewer checklist:

- [ ] Spot-check a few rows of each generated table against the component's `--help` at its pinned tag
- [ ] Provenance lines render correctly on each reworked page (Mintlify preview)
- [ ] `-check` semantics in `scripts/gen-flags/README.md` read sensibly, including the residual-gap list
- [ ] The op-reth pointer page and the six re-pointed inbound links land where expected

## Mintlify automation (replaces the op-batcher-only prompt posted on #21847)

Placeholders below are written as `{component}` (angle brackets do not survive the PR API); substitute the component name.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Name** | Flag reference refresh (op-batcher, op-node, op-proposer, op-challenger, op-conductor) |
| **Trigger** | Custom schedule — `0 9 * * 1` (Mondays 09:00 UTC) |
| **Context repositories** | `ethereum-optimism/optimism` |
| **Integrations** | GitHub (default) |
| **Apply mode** | Require review |

**Additional prompt:**

```
For each covered component — op-batcher, op-node, op-proposer, op-challenger, op-conductor — check the newest finalized release tag (pattern {component}/vX.Y.Z, excluding any -rc or pre-release) in the context repository and compare it against that component's tag recorded in docs/public-docs/scripts/gen-flags/manifest.json. If they all match, do nothing. For each component with a newer finalized tag: regenerate its flag reference per docs/public-docs/scripts/gen-flags/README.md at that tag (go run ./docs/public-docs/scripts/gen-flags -only {component}; if the environment cannot check out the tag, first verify the flag-defining packages listed in the README are unchanged between the tag and the default branch, then generate). Update the generated snippet, the component's manifest.json entry (tag and sha256), and its provenance line together, and propose the change for review. Never hand-edit the generated tables. Never regenerate from unreleased code. If generation fails for one component, still process the others, and describe the failure instead of guessing.
```
